action_prs.scope: Re-run the baseline local arms with the current image and commit the records. Read each failure with tools/trace-evaluate.py: unsafe-point names a predicate and its anchor; model-incomplete names a model gap; evidence-insufficient names the missing trace. Close an arm only when its committed record reads safe.
Build and pin a prior image for the mixed fleet, set RNODE_OLD_IMAGE, and run RC-7's local mixed-store arm.

Bring up the four-host public fleet on a coordinated new genesis, perform the deploy and the single-validator restart through tools/fleet-run.py, and run RC-1/public and RC-4/public on the candidate. The source set and the N1/N4/N8 differential are recorded as diagnostics in the same campaign record; the remaining public arms keep this campaign as their next PR.
One bond/leave campaign feeds RC-1 bond-leave, RC-2 validator-set and RC-4 returner.
Run the pre-registered M3 two-host join and record RC-6 off-host, including the loopback negative.
Add an ordered seed list to bootstrap resolution and run RC-4 failover with the first seed down.
Add the multi-host driver the M4 runbook owes, run N=4 and N=8 on declared hosts, and record RC-2/RC-4 multi-host from the one campaign.
Inject an equivocation under a validator key on the M4 topology, add the finality coordinate, and record RC-2 equivocation.
Drive one deploy id through HTTP, direct HTTP, gRPC and a proxy and record RC-5 transport.
Roll the public fleet through the mixed window to the new image and record RC-7 public.
Aggregate the required arms and the external obligations into the launch gate; refuse ready while any external item is open without a dated disposition.

rule: Each claim names exactly one executable test under tests/ and one or more arms. An arm is a named behaviour with its own environment, evidence locality, test mode and next PR. The tracker stores no status and no missing observation: an arm's status is derived from its newest committed run record by re-running the test's pure check(record), dispatched on the record's arm. A claim whose test does not exist, does not import, or does not define run/check/fixture/CLAIM_ID is refused.
